newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Kosovo guerrilla shot dead by Serb police, Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Kosovo guerrilla shot dead by Serb police, Tanjug.

text.p: A suspected leader of the outlawed Liberation Army of Kosovo was killed in a gunbattle with Serbian police, the official Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported on Saturday.
Quoting the Serbian interior ministry, it said three police officers were wounded in the incident near the town of Vucitrn in Serbian-ruled Kosovo province on Friday.

Tanjug identified the guerrilla as 34-year-old Zahir Pajaziti, adding that two male passengers in the car he was driving were also killed. Police tried to stop the car, were shot at and then returned fire, the agency added.
Independent accounts of what happened were not immediately available.

The shooting follows what ethnic Albanian politicians say is a week-long series of heavy-handed Serbian police raids, ostensibly seeking guerrilla arms, in which at least 37 political activists and humanitarian workers are alleged to have been arrested.
Kosovo has long been seen by many Western political observers as a tinder-box of communal tensions that could upset international peacemaking efforts in the Balkans.
In 1989, Serbia's autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic removed Kosovo's autonomy on the grounds that the region's ethnic Albanian majority were preparing to secede.
Kosovo's ethnic Albanian politicians have tried to stay at arm's length from months of street protests by Serbian students and opposition parties demanding political reforms.
The clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army is reported to have been behind several guerrilla attacks over the past year in which a number of ethnic Albanians and Serbians have died.
